The online RL construction does not justify conformal validity. The purported theoretical analysis is only an algebraic description of a weighted loss. The claimed domain shifts are predominantly synthetic Gaussian corruption of subsets of the same training and test datasets, while the RL environments are small fully observable gridworlds. The experiments do not isolate the claimed contribution. There is no tuned static guidance coefficient, matched-average constant weight, or adequately controlled nonconformal confidence gate. Consequently, the large KD gains may simply arise from downweighting an intentionally poor teacher; several results only recover approximately the from-scratch student performance.

Hyperparameters appear to be selected using reported test accuracy because no separate validation protocol is specified. SSL baselines are also unusually weak and trained for only 51,200 iterations despite claims of following established protocols, without convergence checks or explanation.

The claimed universal framework is instead a collection of materially different, partly ad hoc mechanisms. The appendix provides only a tautological gradient-reweighting illustration, contains a derivative error in Eq. 8, and offers no result connecting conformal coverage to improved learning. Missing implementation details and code further limit reproducibility. These issues invalidate the paper's principal technical and empirical claims rather than constituting minor omissions.
